newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's unemployment falls to 9.5 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: Canada's unemployment falls to 9.5 pct in May.

text.p: Statistics Canada said on Friday the unemployment rate fell to 9.5 percent in May from 9.6 percent in April.
Note - Labor force, employment and unemployment in millions, on seasonally adjusted basis.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast on average that the unemployment rate would show a drop to 9.45 percent.
Full-time employment rose by 70,300 from the month before, while part-time employment fell by 9,000.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast overall employment to grow by 34,700.
Statistics Canada said the unemployment rate only edged down slightly despite strong job gains, mainly because the labor force grew by 50,500 as the number of jobs grew.
The number of jobs has grown by 156,000 since February, representing the strongest three-month gain since 1994, StatsCan said.
Recent job gains have gone entirely to adults (+1.4 percent) since February. In May, employment among adults rose by 71,000 with the gain almost entirely in full-time work, the federal agency said.

But youth employment changed little in May and remained 62,000 or three percent below last year's level, the agency said. The unemployment rate for people aged 15 to 24 was 17.2 percent in May, up 0.2 percentage points from April and 1.7 percentage points from a year ago.

The agency said older students entering the labor market in May in search of a summer job met with difficult conditions. The employment rate of 20 to 24-year-olds was down by 5.3 percentage points to 54.3 percent while unemployment rose 4.3 points to 19.3 percent.
By sector, employment in community, business and personal services rose by 76,000, with the gains mainly in business and personal services, StatsCan said.

Employment in the goods sector changed little in May. In construction, employment fell by 14,000, but in other primary industries employment was up 8,000 in May. Jobs in manufacturing held steady for the second consecutive month following a strong gain in March, the agency said.
Private sector employment grew by 52,000 in May, about half of whom were self-employed. Public sector employment has hardly budged for almost a year, StatsCan said.

Statistics Canada says its employment number should have a margin of error of 62,000 95 percent of the time, or 32,000 at 67 percent of the time. Its unemployment number should have a margin of error of 46,000 95 percent of the time or 24,000 67 percent of the time.
